title: Nārada Muni
summary: The travelling sage whose songs and counsel turn hearts toward devotion and who guides Dhruva, Prahlāda and Vyāsa.
body:
Nārada is a great sage who travels through the universe singing the glories of Lord Nārāyaṇa, accompanied by his vīṇā. He is described as a mind-born son of Brahmā.

He appears again and again in the Bhāgavatam at the moment someone is ready to be guided. He instructs the young Dhruva how to worship the Lord, teaches Prahlāda while Prahlāda is still in his mother's womb, and urges Vyāsadeva to describe the Lord's pastimes directly.

Nārada also tells the story of his own earlier life, when he was the son of a maidservant and received the mercy of saintly devotees.

title: Prahlāda Mahārāja
summary: A young prince whose steady devotion survives his father's cruelty and becomes an example for others.
body:
Prahlāda was born as the son of the demon king Hiraṇyakaśipu, who hated Lord Viṣṇu. While Prahlāda was still in the womb, the sage Nārada taught his mother about devotion, and the child heard it.

As a boy, Prahlāda spoke openly to his schoolmates about devotion to the Lord and said that one should begin early, since human life is short and uncertain.

His father tried many ways to harm him, but Prahlāda remained calm and unafraid. When the Lord appeared as Nṛsiṁha, Prahlāda offered prayers and, when offered any boon, asked only to be free from material desires.

title: Dhruva Mahārāja
summary: A prince who leaves home after a slight, performs severe austerity, and is granted a lasting place in the cosmos.
body:
Dhruva was the son of King Uttānapāda and his queen Sunīti. Hurt by the harsh words of his stepmother Suruci, he went to his mother, who advised him to take shelter of the Supreme Lord.

He set out for the forest, met Nārada, and was guided to practise severe austerities on the bank of the Yamunā at Madhuvana.

When the Lord appeared before him, Dhruva realised that he no longer wanted what he had come to ask for. He later ruled with devotion and attained the abode known as Dhruvaloka.

title: Ambarīṣa Mahārāja
summary: A righteous king whose simple, steady surrender humbles a proud sage and protects his people.
body:
Ambarīṣa was a great emperor who lived a life of complete devotion. He engaged his mind, speech, hands and senses in service to the Lord, and he regularly observed the vow of Ekādaśī and Dvādaśī.

His best-known pastime is his meeting with the powerful sage Durvāsā, in which the Lord's Sudarśana cakra protected Ambarīṣa and taught Durvāsā that the Lord is bound by the love of his devotees.

title: Vyāsadeva
summary: The compiler who gathers the ancient Vedic knowledge into lasting forms and teaches the path of devotion to his son.
body:
Vyāsadeva, also known as Veda-Vyāsa, divided the Vedic knowledge into parts so that people could study it, and composed the Purāṇas and the Mahābhārata.

Even after all this work he felt unsatisfied. Nārada explained that he had not yet described the Lord's glories directly. Following this advice, Vyāsa meditated, and then composed the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, which he taught to his son Śukadeva.

title: Śukadeva Gosvāmī
summary: A detached sage who narrates the Lord's pastimes to a dying king and awakens faith in his final hours.
body:
Śukadeva was the son of Vyāsadeva and lived as a completely detached wanderer. He studied the Bhāgavatam under his father.

He arrived on the bank of the Gaṅgā where King Parīkṣit was sitting, preparing for death, and when asked what a person about to die should hear, he narrated the Bhāgavatam to the king.

title: Parīkṣit Mahārāja
summary: An emperor who accepts a curse, renounces his throne, and spends his last seven days hearing the Lord's pastimes.
body:
Parīkṣit was a righteous emperor and a grandson of Arjuna. After a sage's son cursed him to die within seven days, he accepted the curse calmly, handed over his kingdom, and sat on the bank of the Gaṅgā.

His sincere question to Śukadeva Gosvāmī about what a dying person should hear became the occasion for the narration of the entire Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.

title: Arjuna
summary: The Pāṇḍava archer who receives Kṛṣṇa's counsel on the battlefield after his resolve fails.
body:
Arjuna was one of the five Pāṇḍava brothers, a great archer, and a close friend and cousin of Kṛṣṇa.

At the start of the great war at Kurukṣetra he was overcome by confusion and grief at the sight of his relatives in the opposing army. He accepted Kṛṣṇa as his teacher, and Kṛṣṇa spoke the Bhagavad-gītā to him.

title: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu
summary: The Vaiṣṇava saint whose life and teaching inspire the Vraja Gosvāmīs and the Gauḍīya path.
body:
Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is the guru and inspiration of the Vṛndāvana Gosvāmīs. He personally instructed Sanātana Gosvāmī for two months in Vārāṇasī, directly empowered Rūpa Gosvāmī, and is accepted in Gauḍīya traditions as the guru of Gadādhara Paṇḍita, Lokanātha and Bhūgarbha.

He is also described as delighting in Jayadeva's Gīta Govinda at Jagannātha Purī. Jayadeva lived centuries earlier and was not historically part of the Gauḍīya paramparā.

relations.role: Recipient of later association and blessings
Relished his Gīta Govinda in Jagannātha Purī

title: Madhva
summary: The early Vedānta teacher who stands at the beginning of the lineage followed in Vraja.
body: Madhva is named at the head of the lineage that passes through Mādhavendra Purī, Īśvara Purī and Śrī Caitanya to the Vraja Gosvāmīs. Vraja tradition list him as the earlier authority in the line; they do not describe a direct initiation of Mādhavendra by him.

title: Mādhavendra Purī
summary: A saintly renunciate in the line between Madhva and Īśvara Purī, remembered for tender devotion.
body: Mādhavendra Purī is listed after Madhva and before Īśvara Purī in the Gauḍīya paramparā.

title: Īśvara Purī
summary: The renounced guru who initiates Caitanya and carries the lineage forward.
body: Īśvara Purī stands between Mādhavendra Purī and Śrī Caitanya in the lineage list. He is named as the dīkṣā-guru of Mahāprabhu.

title: Sanātana Gosvāmī
summary: A Gosvāmī instructed by Caitanya in Vārāṇasī and linked with the Madana-mohana deity.
body:
Sanātana Gosvāmī is named as the main Gosvāmī connected with the Madana-mohana temple. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is accepted as both his dīkṣā- and śikṣā-guru.

Mahāprabhu personally instructed him for two months in Vārāṇasī. Lineage: Madhva → Mādhavendra Purī → Īśvara Purī → Śrī Caitanya → Sanātana Gosvāmī.

In the traditional Gaura–Kṛṣṇa correspondence, Sanātana Gosvāmī is connected with Rati-mañjarī, Laṅga-mañjarī and Sanātana Kumāra.

title: Rūpa Gosvāmī
summary: A Gosvāmī who shaped Gauḍīya theology and served the Govindadeva deity in Vraja.
body:
Rūpa Gosvāmī is named as the main Gosvāmī connected with the Govindadeva temple. He received direct empowerment and theological instructions from Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, including teachings later expressed in Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu.

Lineage: Madhva → Mādhavendra Purī → Īśvara Purī → Śrī Caitanya → Rūpa Gosvāmī.

In the traditional Gaura–Kṛṣṇa correspondence, Rūpa Gosvāmī is connected with Rūpa-mañjarī.

title: Gadādhara Paṇḍita
summary: A learned associate and disciple of Caitanya, honoured as a teacher in the Gaura circle.
body:
Gadādhara Paṇḍita is given as the dīkṣā-guru of Mādhupandita, the Gosvāmī connected with the Gopīnātha temple. Within Gaura-līlā he is accepted as a direct disciple and associate of Śrī Caitanya.

In the traditional Gaura–Kṛṣṇa correspondence, Gadādhara Paṇḍita is connected with Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's pleasure potency, Lalitā, and Hari.

title: Mādhupandita Gosvāmī
summary: The Gosvāmī linked with the Gopīnātha deity and with Gadādhara Paṇḍita's line.
body:
Mādhupandita is named as the main Gosvāmī connected with Śrī Rādhā-Gopīnātha. His dīkṣā-guru was Gadādhara Paṇḍita.

Lineage: Madhva → Mādhavendra Purī → Īśvara Purī → Śrī Caitanya → Gadādhara Paṇḍita → Mādhupandita.

title: Jīva Gosvāmī
summary: The theologian who organized Gauḍīya thought and cared for the Rādhā-Dāmodara deity.
body:
Jīva Gosvāmī is named as the main Gosvāmī connected with the Rādhā-Dāmodara temple. Rūpa Gosvāmī, his uncle, was his dīkṣā-guru. He is considered the principal systematizer of Gauḍīya theology.

Lineage: Madhva → Mādhavendra Purī → Īśvara Purī → Śrī Caitanya → Rūpa Gosvāmī → Jīva Gosvāmī.

In the traditional Gaura–Kṛṣṇa correspondence, Jīva Gosvāmī is connected with Vilāsa-mañjarī.

title: Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī
summary: The elderly Gosvāmī who wrote the life of Caitanya while living at Rādhā-Dāmodara.
body:
Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī is famous for composing Caitanya-caritāmṛta. He lived and wrote at Rādhā-Dāmodara in Vṛndāvana.

His dīkṣā-guru and śikṣā-guru were Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī. He also drew inspiration from Svarūpa Dāmodara. In his later years he wrote Caitanya-caritāmṛta at Rādhā-Dāmodara, systematizing the theology of Rūpa and Raghunātha.

Lineage: Madhva → Mādhavendra Purī → Īśvara Purī → Śrī Caitanya → Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī → Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja.

title: Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī
summary: A renounced Gosvāmī who guided Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja and stands in the line of Caitanya's associates.
body:
Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī is listed after Śrī Caitanya in the lineage that reaches Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja. Vraja tradition name him as both the dīkṣā- and śikṣā-guru of Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja, who composed Caitanya-caritāmṛta.

In the traditional Gaura–Kṛṣṇa correspondence, Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī is connected with Rasa-mañjarī, Rati-mañjarī and Bhānumatī.

title: Svarūpa Dāmodara
summary: Caitanya's intimate companion whose presence shaped Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja's writing.
body: Svarūpa Dāmodara inspired Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja, alongside the direct guidance of Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī.

title: Jayadeva
summary: A poet from an earlier age whose songs on Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa were cherished by Caitanya; no initiation link is claimed.
body:
Jayadeva lived in the 12th century, centuries before Mahāprabhu, and was not part of the Gauḍīya paramparā historically. His Gīta Govinda nevertheless deeply influenced Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who regularly heard and relished it in Jagannātha Purī.

There is no dīkṣā connection to Caitanya. He is better understood as a previous ācārya in the rāgānugā-bhakti current whose mood was later embraced in Gauḍīya teaching.

relations.role: Relished Gīta Govinda in Jagannātha Purī; no dīkṣā link

title: Bhūgarbha Gosvāmī
summary: A renounced companion of Lokanātha who helped locate and restore sacred sites in Vraja.
body:
Bhūgarbha Gosvāmī is described as a close associate of Lokanātha Gosvāmī. He assisted in discovering holy places in Vṛndāvana and lived in deep renunciation, helping to establish early Vraja bhajana sites.

Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is traditionally accepted as his dīkṣā-guru. Lineage: Madhva → Mādhavendra Purī → Īśvara Purī → Śrī Caitanya → Bhūgarbha Gosvāmī.

title: Lokanātha Gosvāmī
summary: The Gosvāmī linked with Rādhā-Gokulānanda and the teacher of Narottama Dāsa Ṭhākura.
body:
Lokanātha Gosvāmī is the Gosvāmī connected with the Rādhā-Gokulānanda temple, where the deities include Vijaya Govinda and Rādhā-Vinoda. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu is traditionally accepted as his dīkṣā-guru.

Narottama Dāsa Ṭhākura is named as his famous disciple. Bhūgarbha Gosvāmī was his close associate in discovering holy places in Vraja.

Lineage: Madhva → Mādhavendra Purī → Īśvara Purī → Śrī Caitanya → Lokanātha Gosvāmī.

title: Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī
summary: The Gosvāmī associated with the self-manifested Rādhā-Ramaṇa deity.
body:
Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī is named as the main Gosvāmī connected with the Rādhā-Ramaṇa temple, whose deity is described as self-manifested from a śālagrāma.

Prabodhānanda Sarasvatī is traditionally accepted as his dīkṣā-guru. Vraja tradition also record later association and blessings from Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

Lineage: Madhva → Mādhavendra Purī → Īśvara Purī → Śrī Caitanya → Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī.

In the traditional Gaura–Kṛṣṇa correspondence, Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī is connected with Aṅgana-mañjarī and Guṇa-mañjarī.

title: Prabodhānanda Sarasvatī
summary: A respected teacher traditionally accepted as Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī's initiation guru.
body: Prabodhānanda Sarasvatī is named in Vraja tradition as the dīkṣā-guru of Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī, with the qualification 'traditionally accepted'.

title: Śyāmānanda Prabhu
summary: The Gosvāmī connected with the Rādhā-Śyāmasundara deity and the line of Hṛdaya Caitanya.
body:
Śyāmānanda Prabhu is named as the main Gosvāmī connected with Śrī Rādhā-Śyāmasundara. His dīkṣā-guru was Hṛdaya Caitanya.

Lineage: Madhva → Mādhavendra Purī → Īśvara Purī → Śrī Caitanya → Gauridāsa Paṇḍita → Hṛdaya Caitanya → Śyāmānanda.

title: Hṛdaya Caitanya
summary: The teacher who stands before Śyāmānanda Prabhu in the Rādhā-Śyāmasundara lineage.
body: Hṛdaya Caitanya is listed as the dīkṣā-guru of Śyāmānanda Prabhu and as a disciple of Gauridāsa Paṇḍita.

title: Gauridāsa Paṇḍita
summary: A teacher in that same line, linked through a guru who directly knew Caitanya.
body: Gauridāsa Paṇḍita appears between Śrī Caitanya's immediate circle and Hṛdaya Caitanya in the lineage given for the Rādhā-Śyāmasundara temple. Vraja tradition say that Gauridāsa's guru was a direct associate of Śrī Caitanya; they do not name that associate.

title: Narottama Dāsa Ṭhākura
summary: A devoted disciple of Lokanātha Gosvāmī who carried the Vraja tradition forward.
body: Narottama Dāsa Ṭhākura is named in Vraja tradition as the famous disciple of Lokanātha Gosvāmī, the Gosvāmī connected with Rādhā-Gokulānanda.

title: Vajranābha
summary: The figure credited in tradition with setting up sixteen principal deities throughout Vraja Maṇḍala.
body:
Vajranābha is traditionally credited with installing at least sixteen important deities at sacred spots in and around Vraja Maṇḍala, including purāṇic descriptions linked to the Ādi-Varāha Purāṇa and Vraja lore.

The set is described as four principal Devas, four Gopāla forms, four Śiva liṅgas (Dik-pālas), and four Devīs. These installations are associated with places such as Vṛndāvana, Mathurā, Govardhana and Kāmyavana.

This entry is a draft summary of Vraja tradition rather than an independently verified historical survey.

title: Acyutānanda
summary: A son of Advaita Ācārya who appears in the household circle of the Gaura pastimes.
body:
Acyutānanda is named among the branches connected with Advaita Ācārya's household. He belongs to the close circle that grew around Śrī Caitanya's family line.

In the traditional Gaura–Kṛṣṇa correspondence, Acyutānanda is linked with Acyutā-devī and Kārttikeya.

title: Advaita Ācārya
summary: The senior associate of Caitanya who taught in Navadvīpa and hosted the early devotees.
body:
Advaita Ācārya stands near the centre of the Gaura pastimes as a senior companion of Śrī Caitanya and a respected householder teacher. His household becomes a meeting point for many of the later branches.

He is understood as Sadāśiva and Mahā-Viṣṇu in the Vraja–Gaura correspondence.

title: Akincana Kṛṣṇadāsa
summary: A poet-devotee whose verses express surrender within Caitanya's circle.
body: Akincana Kṛṣṇadāsa appears in the line of devotees who kept the memory of Śrī Caitanya alive through song and service. His place is modest, but firmly within the extended family of the Gaura pastimes.

title: Anupama Mallikā
summary: A woman devotee remembered among the close associates in the Gaura pastimes.
body: Anupama Mallikā is remembered among the women whose lives were drawn into the Gaura pastimes. Her name is preserved as one of the branches surrounding Śrī Caitanya's circle.

title: Bhagavān Paṇḍita
summary: A learned devotee who took part in Caitanya's gatherings.
body:
Bhagavān Paṇḍita is named among the Paṇḍitas connected with Śrī Caitanya. He appears in the wider company of devotees who carried the Gaura pastimes forward.

He is described as a śaktyāveśa manifestation in the Gaura pastimes.

title: Bhāgavata Ācārya
summary: A teacher and reciter counted among Caitanya's branches.
body: Bhāgavata Ācārya belongs to the line of teachers associated with the Gaura pastimes. The tradition remembers him as one of the branches around Śrī Caitanya.

title: Buddhimanta Khān
summary: A householder associate known for service in Navadvīpa's devotee community.
body: Buddhimanta Khān is counted among the householders who belonged to Śrī Caitanya's wider circle. His name survives in the lists of the Gaura branches.

title: Caitanya Dāsa
summary: A servant-devotee whose name reflects dedication to Caitanya.
body:
Caitanya Dāsa is remembered as a devoted servant within the extended company of Śrī Caitanya. His name appears among the branches of the Gaura pastimes.

He is linked with Dakṣa, Kṛṣṇa's parrot, in the traditional correspondence.

title: Candraśekhara Ācārya
summary: A learned companion who appears beside Caitanya in Navadvīpa.
body:
Candraśekhara Ācārya is remembered as one of the learned companions who gathered around Śrī Caitanya. He shares in the intimate atmosphere of the Gaura pastimes.

He is identified with Soma-deva, the moon god.

title: Cirañjīva
summary: A devotee listed among the branches growing from Caitanya's presence.
body:
Cirañjīva appears among the devotees connected with the Gaura pastimes. Little is said here beyond his place in that circle.

He is linked with Candrikā in the traditional correspondence.

title: Dāmodara Paṇḍita
summary: A close Navadvīpa associate who served Caitanya in His early years.
body:
Dāmodara Paṇḍita is remembered among the learned householders who moved closely with Śrī Caitanya. He belongs to the intimate Navadvīpa circle.

He is connected with Saibyā-devī and Goddess Sarasvatī.

title: Gadādhara Dāsa
summary: A devotee connected with the Gadādhara line in the Gaura pastimes.
body:
Gadādhara Dāsa is named among the branches associated with Gadādhara's company. He is kept distinct here from Gadādhara Paṇḍita, who has his own entry.

He is linked with Candrakāntī and Purānānanda-devī.

title: Gaṅgādāsa Paṇḍita
summary: A Paṇḍita known among Caitanya's early companions.
body:
Gaṅgādāsa Paṇḍita is named among the Paṇḍitas connected with Śrī Caitanya. He stands in the wider company of Gaura's associates.

He is identified with Durvāsā Muni.

title: Garuḍa Paṇḍita
summary: A devotee whose service and learning placed him in Caitanya's circle.
body:
Garuḍa Paṇḍita appears among the branches of the Gaura pastimes. His name carries a clear link with the bird carrier of Viṣṇu.

He is identified with Garuḍa, the carrier of Viṣṇu.

title: Gopāla Dāsa
summary: A member of Advaita Ācārya's household, counted among the Gaura branches.
body:
Gopāla Dāsa is named as one of the sons in Advaita Ācārya's household. He therefore belongs to the family circle that surrounded Śrī Caitanya.

He is connected with Gaṇeśa.

title: Gopālaguru Gosvāmī
summary: A Gosvāmī remembered among the later branches of Caitanya's tree.
body: Gopālaguru Gosvāmī appears in the line of Gosvāmīs associated with the Gaura pastimes. His place is recorded among the later branches.

title: Gopīnātha Siṁha
summary: A devotee who appears in the wider network of Caitanya's associates.
body:
Gopīnātha Siṁha is counted among the associates connected with Śrī Caitanya. He belongs to the wider network of Gaura's branches.

He is identified with Akrūra.

title: Govinda Datta
summary: A householder devotee who supported the early Navadvīpa gatherings.
body: Govinda Datta is remembered among the householders in Śrī Caitanya's circle. His name is preserved in the lists of the Gaura branches.

title: Govindānanda
summary: A companion who shared in Caitanya's pastimes in Navadvīpa.
body:
Govindānanda appears among the close associates of the Gaura pastimes. He is remembered as one of Śrī Caitanya's branches.

He is linked with Sugrīva in the Rāma-līlā correspondence.

title: Haridāsa Ṭhākura
summary: The great singer of the holy name, honoured as the Nāma-ācārya of the Gaura circle.
body:
Haridāsa Ṭhākura is revered for unwavering chanting of the holy name. His steady practice makes him one of the most recognizable figures in the Gaura circle.

He is connected with Brahmā, Prahlāda and Mahātapā.

title: Hiraṇya Paṇḍita
summary: A Paṇḍita counted among the learned devotees around Caitanya.
body:
Hiraṇya Paṇḍita is named among the Paṇḍitas connected with Śrī Caitanya. He appears in the company of the Gaura branches.

He is linked with one of the brāhmaṇa wives who offered food to Kṛṣṇa.

title: Jagadānanda Paṇḍita
summary: A scholar-devotee who served Caitanya and helped spread His teaching.
body:
Jagadānanda Paṇḍita is remembered among the learned companions of Śrī Caitanya. He stands close to the central Gaura circle.

He is identified with Satyabhāmā.

title: Jagadīśa Paṇḍita
summary: A close companion in the early Gaura pastimes.
body:
Jagadīśa Paṇḍita appears among the devotees closely tied to Śrī Caitanya. His name is kept among the principal branches.

He is linked with Candrāhasā and a wife of Kaliya.

title: Kamalākānta Viśvāsa
summary: A householder devotee associated with the wider Gaura circle.
body: Kamalākānta Viśvāsa is remembered among the extended associates of Śrī Caitanya. His name is preserved as one of the branches.

title: Kavi Karṇapūra
summary: A poet-devotee remembered for his writings on Kṛṣṇa's pastimes.
body: Kavi Karṇapūra is remembered as a poet who praised the Gaura pastimes. He belongs to the company that kept Śrī Caitanya's memory vivid.

title: Kholāvecā Śrīdhara
summary: A Navadvīpa householder known for supplying oil to the devotees.
body:
Kholāvecā Śrīdhara is named among the householders connected with Śrī Caitanya. His place is within the Navadvīpa circle.

He is identified with Kusumāsava.

title: Kṛṣṇa Miśra
summary: A son in Advaita Ācārya's family who appears among Caitanya's branches.
body:
Kṛṣṇa Miśra is named as a son in Advaita Ācārya's household. That places him among the family branches of the Gaura pastimes.

He is linked with Kārttikeya.

title: Mādhvācārya
summary: A teacher listed among those who received Caitanya's mercy.
body:
Mādhvācārya appears among the teachers associated with Śrī Caitanya. He is counted in the wider line of Gaura's branches.

He is identified with Mādhavī-devī.

title: Makaradhvaja Kara
summary: A poet-devotee whose verses are associated with the Gaura circle.
body:
Makaradhvaja Kara is remembered among the devotees who served the Gaura pastimes with poetry and song.

He is linked with Sukeshī and Candramukha.

title: Mukunda Dāsa
summary: A dedicated servant counted among Caitanya's early followers.
body:
Mukunda Dāsa appears among the associates of Śrī Caitanya. He is kept distinct from Mukunda Datta, who has a separate entry.

He is identified with Vṛndā-devī.

title: Mukunda Datta
summary: A close associate who shared Caitanya's childhood and later pastimes.
body:
Mukunda Datta is remembered as one of the close companions in the Gaura pastimes. His name appears among the principal branches.

He is linked with Madhukānta.

title: Murāri Gupta
summary: A physician-devotee who served Caitanya and witnessed His early manifestations.
body:
Murāri Gupta is remembered as a devoted servant and an early witness of Śrī Caitanya's life. His closeness to the Navadvīpa circle makes him a reliable point of reference.

He is identified with Hanumān.

title: Nandana Ācārya
summary: An Ācārya named among Caitanya's branches.
body: Nandana Ācārya is counted among the teachers connected with the Gaura pastimes. His name is preserved in the lists of branches.

title: Narahari Sarkāra
summary: A devotee and teacher in the line that followed Caitanya.
body:
